findings.body:
chunk 1/2:

When a user runs `forge close <item>` from an upgraded main checkout while the item's worktree still pins v1.2.42, `repo.check_pin` reads main's pin and returns before calling this dispatcher. The installed close then operates on the older worktree and its `_synced` check refuses the older pin before CI recovery or review. `forge land --all` has the same issue because its children start from main. The new test runs close from the item worktree, so it misses this common entry point.
findings.title: Route close through the target worktree's pinned release

findings.body:
chunk 1/2:

The bridge unconditionally reads `close._synced` and later `close._push`, but released versions do not all provide those helpers. The v1.0.0 close has neither, and v1.2.0 and v1.2.1 push directly without `_push`. Closing a branch pinned to one of those releases therefore raises `AttributeError` during bootstrap, even before review or CI. Existing repos can have these pins; the upgrade test itself uses v1.0.0 as an earlier release.
findings.title: Handle releases without the assumed close helpers

findings.body:
chunk 1/2:

Wrapping `_synced` is too late for older close implementations that merge the default branch first. The released v1.2.2 close always merges main before calling `_synced`, so a normal main upgrade changes the open branch's pin even when the merge has no conflict. The v1.2.42 close also merges main when GitHub reports the PR as behind, then resumes using the newly merged pin. These paths do not preserve the old pin and, in the latter case, can run review through the newer release.
findings.title: Preserve the branch pin before the older close merges main

findings.body:
chunk 2/2:

Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - after main upgrades, a coordinator runs `forge close <item>` from the main checkout for an open v1.2.42 worktree. The upgrade test always invokes close from the older worktree, while the queue test leaves main on the old pin. From upgraded main, `src/forge/repo.py:937-939` returns before dispatching the pinned release, and `src/forge/close.py:801-811` refuses the worktree's unchanged pin before review or CI recovery. The named proof therefore passes while this upgrade path still fails. Exercise the command from upgraded main and require the pinned review and installed CI recovery.
findings.title: Gate: cover closing an older worktree from upgraded main

why: A branch pinned to the earlier release runs close and merge through that release, so CI-wait fixes in a newer installed release (rerun failed groups, cancelled is not failed) do not apply until each branch merges the pin upgrade
